subtype: Approach: assume skills transfer without checking [Pitfall]
passage:
Day 1. Over tea, Lalit tells Vijay, "Twenty-five kids in a room and I can hold every one of them. Sales is just talking." The company's product-training video stays unwatched.

Day 9. The target sheet says forty calls a day. Lalit's first cold call ends in a click after eight seconds. So does the second. Explaining everything patiently, the way it works in a classroom, gets nowhere when the listener can simply hang up. By evening Lalit has booked no visits at all.

Day 21. Lalit is far behind on targets. Vijay says, "You never asked what the job needed." Lalit opens a notebook and writes two columns: what I assumed, and what actually happened. The second column is much longer.

qa.q: How many calls a day did the target sheet require?
qa.a: The target sheet said forty calls a day.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling after the first cold call ended in a click?
qa.a: Lalit felt surprised and rattled, because the confidence from the classroom did not work on a stranger who could hang up.

qa.q: What could Lalit have done before the first day to test the assumption?
qa.a: Lalit could have listened in on a senior's calls or practised a few mock cold calls, so the gaps showed up early instead of against targets.

qa.q: How might Vijay see Lalit's plan?
qa.a: Vijay may see it as confident but untested, and may feel concerned watching Lalit skip the training video and then fall behind.

grounding: Illustrates a teacher moving into sales who assumes classroom skills will transfer and is caught out by targets and cold-calling.
